messages:
maria: FYI Pulse reported a sudden TPS surge against their dedicated pool around 20:03-20:08 UTC. Customers saw 429s and 200-500ms extra latency. Also getting a couple reports of intermittent 401s and billing shows burst credits stayed flat during the spike :confused:

anya: Can you paste the pool_id and a sample request_id so we can trace?

maria: pool_id=pulse-ded-7, sample request_ids: req_3f9a2b, req_3f9a7c. Logs attached below (snips).

maria: ```
[20:03:12] admission: reject token request_id=req_3f9a2b reason=burst_credits_exhausted headroom=0.12 target_tps=120 current_tps=420
[20:03:13] proxy: upstream_latency=220ms status=429 request_id=req_3f9a2b
[20:04:01] auth: upstream returned 401 for token=redacted request_id=req_3f9a7c
```

tom: Thanks. Two immediate asks: 1) can we reproduce load pattern? 2) query autoscaler and admission control metrics for that pool (pending queue, headroom multiplier, burst_credit_balance).

kai: Pulling metrics now. Quick read: the autoscaler did execute, but added nodes after a 90s delay due to the scaling cooldown. Admission controller uses a headroom multiplier of 0.15 for this pool; during the spike our observed incoming token rate jumped from ~110 TPS to ~430 TPS in <30s which crossed the admission threshold before new workers came up. Also saw burst_credits_balance = 0 for pool (billing log shows consumption wasn't recorded).

maria: Repro steps (what Pulse did): ramp from 50 -> 450 TPS over 25s, sustained ~2 min. They used 8 concurrent clients each doing short-generation calls (~20 tokens). We ran a quick local repro with this curl + xargs load:

maria: ```bash
for i in $(seq 1 450); do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $PULSE_KEY" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/dedicated/pool/pulse-ded-7/generate\" -d '{"prompt":"test"}' &
  if (( i % 8 == 0 )); then wait; fi
 done
```

tom: That matches the window. The 401s are strange — maybe token validation timing out behind the auth-cache when proxy retries fail. Can we get proxy->auth call traces for those request_ids?

maria: Sent to #eng-runtime, but logs show auth svc returning 200 for most requests, 401 for a handful exactly when the proxy returned 429s. Possibly client retried with expired token. Pulse denies any client-side change.

billing-bot: internal_billing.lookup(pool_id=pulse-ded-7, window=20:00-20:10) -> burst_credits_start=500, burst_credits_used=0, burst_credits_end=500 (anomaly flagged)

kai: Looks like a separate accounting pipeline lag — the charge emitter fell behind under load, so credits weren't decremented even though admission counted them as used. That caused admission to hit a safety gate (credits exhausted) while billing shows full balance. We need to reconcile and refund credits post-hoc and fix emitter backpressure handling.

anya: For the customer: propose immediate mitigation steps we can run now?

kai: Short-term mitigations we can apply to pulse-ded-7: 1) increase admission headroom multiplier from 0.15 -> 0.25 for 30m (manual override) 2) temporarily disable burst-credit gating for this pool (failsafe) 3) prewarm + add 2 nodes to pool immediately. I'll run 1 & 3 now.

kai: Applying: `PATCH /internal/pools/pulse-ded-7/config {"headroom_multiplier":0.25}` -> :gear:

deploy-bot: rollout pulse-ded-7 config patch succeeded in 3 zones at 20:28 UTC

kai: Manually adding nodes: `POST /internal/autoscaler/force_add?pool=pulse-ded-7&count=2` -> success. Latency and 429s falling within 60s.

maria: Confirmed with Pulse: 429s dropped to near zero and p95 latency returned to baseline. Customer also reports no further 401s in subsequent checks. :relieved:

billing-bot: reconciled usage: burst_credits_used=430 (reconciled) burst_credits_end=70. Adjusted customer invoice; issuing internal credit to cover the window due to emitter lag.

tom: Root causes we see so far: 1) extremely fast TPS ramp that outran autoscaler cooldown, 2) admission control headroom was too tight for this workload pattern, 3) billing/emitter lag caused a mismatch between admission accounting and billing state (admission blocked because local counter believed credits exhausted), 4) transient auth failures likely due to proxy retries during overload.

anya: Customer comms drafted: explain we applied emergency headroom increase and prewarm, reconciled credits and issued credit, and we're doing a postmortem + config changes. Send draft to me for review, cc legal for billing language.

maria: Follow-ups / action items: - kai to add autoscaler tuning: decrease cooldown for pools with bursty patterns OR enable predictive prewarm based on recent ramp patterns (ETA 2 weeks). - eng-runtime to add a circuit-breaker for auth proxy retries to reduce 401 noise (tom). - billing to add end-to-end backlog alert when emitter lag > 30s (billing-bot / anya). - add an SLO alert that measures headroom margin < 0.1 for >30s (kai).

kai: I'll also add a guard in the emitter to apply backpressure instead of dropping accounting events; quick patch queued.

tom: For postmortem, please include exact metric graphs (incoming TPS, worker count, admission rejects, burst_credit_local_counter vs billing ledger) and the snippets you pasted. I'll take ownership of the PM and timeline.

maria: Thanks all. Customer notified and happy with quick mitigation. Leaving this thread open until the follow-ups are in place. :white_check_mark:
